# LLMs

> The documentation for AI assistants — every page as Markdown, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, Copy page and Open in Claude or ChatGPT, the type declarations of your version.

These pages are written for people and coding agents alike. Every one of them is also plain Markdown, the whole site is one file, and the package’s types document every export of the version you installed.

## Every page as Markdown

Add `.md` to a page’s address: [`/three-map-terrain/materials/`](/three-map-terrain/materials/) is also [`/three-map-terrain/materials.md`](/three-map-terrain/materials.md). The Markdown is the rendered page flattened — components become their text, a live demo becomes its code — and each page points to it with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`, so agents that look for it find it.

Above every title, **Copy page** puts that Markdown on the clipboard; its menu also opens it as text, or in a new chat in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot or Perplexity.

## llms.txt and llms-full.txt

Following [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org):

| File                                                 | What                                                                      | For                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`/llms.txt`](/three-map-terrain/llms.txt)           | The index: the library in a sentence, then every page with its summary    | An agent that fetches what it needs — give it this address                |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/three-map-terrain/llms-full.txt) | Every page in one Markdown file, in the order of the guide (about 100 KB) | A model with a long context, a tool that indexes docs by URL, offline use |

The guide comes first in both, the reference after it. Prompts that work:

```text
Read https://whidrubeld.github.io/three-map-terrain/llms.txt, then add
OpenStreetMap buildings and roads to the map in src/scene.ts.
```

```text
Using https://whidrubeld.github.io/three-map-terrain/layers/vegetation.md,
plant orchards with low trees on my map.
```

## The API of your version

The pages describe the latest release. The package’s type declarations describe the one you installed — every export with its documentation comment: `node_modules/three-map-terrain/dist/index.d.ts`, or [the latest on unpkg](https://unpkg.com/three-map-terrain/dist/index.d.ts). An agent unsure of an option’s name or a signature should read them before guessing.

## The agent skill

For agents that load skills — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and many more — [the skill](/three-map-terrain/skill/) is this documentation’s essentials in one file: the model, recipes, pitfalls, and where to read more. One command installs it:

```bash
npx skills add whidrubeld/three-map-terrain
```

# Agent skill

> A skill that teaches coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others — the library, installed with npx skills from GitHub, or from the npm package so that it matches your version.

An [agent skill](https://agentskills.io) is a `SKILL.md` a coding agent loads when a task needs it — here, code importing `three-map-terrain`, a real place to show on terrain, a model to print. The skill holds the library’s essentials:

* **The model** — the grid of tiles, Z up, units and true scale, local coordinates, the lifecycle (`init`, `whenReady`, `clean`).
* **Recipes** — three.js and React Three Fiber, positions and picking, a city with its layers, sources, materials, a layer of your own, export, large areas, performance.
* **Pitfalls** — what makes terrain black, invisible or squashed, layers empty, credits missing.
* **Where to read more** — the type declarations of the installed version, and [these pages as Markdown](/three-map-terrain/llms/).

## Install

With the [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI, from this repository — it asks which agents to install it for:

```bash
npx skills add whidrubeld/three-map-terrain
```

Or for one agent, in every project:

```bash
npx skills add whidrubeld/three-map-terrain \
  --skill three-map-terrain -a claude-code -g
```

`npx skills update` brings it up to date, `npx skills remove three-map-terrain` takes it away.

## From the npm package

The package ships the skill too (from the release after 3.5.1): linked from `node_modules`, it matches the version you installed and updates with it. The `skills` CLI’s sync is experimental:

```bash
npm install -D skills
npx skills experimental_sync -y
```

A `prepare` script — `"prepare": "skills experimental_sync -y"` — keeps it linked after every install.

## Without installing

```bash
npx skills use whidrubeld/three-map-terrain@three-map-terrain \
  --agent claude-code
```

starts the agent with the skill; without `--agent` it prints the prompt.

## The skill

[`skills/three-map-terrain/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/whidrubeld/three-map-terrain/blob/master/skills/three-map-terrain/SKILL.md), as installed:

Show the skill

**SKILL.md**

````md
---
name: three-map-terrain
description: Build real-world 3D terrain in three.js or React Three Fiber with the three-map-terrain library — elevation and imagery from map tiles, OpenStreetMap buildings, roads and bridges, water and vegetation, layers of your own (FeatureLayer), materials, picking and geolocation, GLB / STL / USDZ export, streaming and levels of detail. Use when code imports three-map-terrain, or when asked to show a real place, a GPS track or map data on 3D terrain, or to make a terrain model to print.
---

# three-map-terrain

A three.js library: a `Map` loads elevation and imagery tiles around a place
and builds a grid of terrain meshes; layers (buildings, roads, water,
vegetation, a base, yours) are drawn on it from vector tiles, OpenStreetMap
or any data. `three` is a peer dependency (≥ 0.152); TypeScript types ship
with the package.

## Where the truth is

- **The installed version's API**: `node_modules/three-map-terrain/dist/index.d.ts`
  — every export with its TSDoc. Read it for exact signatures and options
  before guessing; check `node_modules/three-map-terrain/package.json` for
  the version.
- **The documentation**, every page also as Markdown (add `.md`):
  <https://whidrubeld.github.io/three-map-terrain/llms.txt> lists them,
  <https://whidrubeld.github.io/three-map-terrain/llms-full.txt> is all of
  them. Pages: `getting-started.md`, `layers.md`, `layers/buildings.md`,
  `layers/roads.md`, `layers/water.md`, `layers/vegetation.md`,
  `layers/base.md`, `own-layers.md`, `materials.md`, `sources.md`,
  `export.md`, `large-areas.md`, `performance.md`, `api/map.md`,
  `api/layers.md`, `api/sources.md`, `api/exports.md` — under
  `https://whidrubeld.github.io/three-map-terrain/`. They describe the latest
  release; the types describe the installed one.

## The model

- `new Map({ location, source?, elevation?, options?, material? })`: a grid
  of tiles at `options.zoom` (default 11) — `nTiles × nTiles` (default 3)
  around `location`, or any rectangle `options.grid`
  (`{ minX, minY, maxX, maxY }` in tiles). `location` is the origin of the
  coordinates either way.
- `map.terrain` is a `Group` — add it to the scene. One mesh per tile, and
  the layers' objects.
- **Z is up**: the terrain lies in the XY plane, X east, Y north. Set
  `camera.up.set(0, 0, 1)` and a far plane of about `1e6`.
- **Units**: a tile is `tileSize` (600) scene units wide; heights are
  `zScale` units per meter. The default `zScale` is true scale only at zoom
  11 around 46°: set `exaggeration: 1` for true scale anywhere (and `> 1` to
  exaggerate). `baseAltitude` (meters) is drawn at z = 0 — keeps a city at
  300 m near the origin.
- **Positions** are in `map.terrain`'s local coordinates; convert with
  `worldToLocal` / `localToWorld` if `map.terrain` or its parents move.
- **Lifecycle**: `await map.init()` resolves when every tile has its heights
  (textures and layers keep streaming in); `map.whenReady()` waits for
  everything; `map.clean()` aborts requests and frees GPU memory — call it on
  unmount (safe with React StrictMode: `init()` again works). Layers survive
  `clean()`.
- Built-in materials are lit (`MeshLambertMaterial`): add an `AmbientLight`
  and a `DirectionalLight`, or pass `material: { lights: false }`.

## Recipes

### A map in three.js

```ts
import {
  AmbientLight,
  DirectionalLight,
  PerspectiveCamera,
  Scene,
  WebGLRenderer
} from 'three'
import { MapControls } from 'three/addons/controls/MapControls.js'
import { Map } from 'three-map-terrain'

const scene = new Scene()
scene.add(new AmbientLight(0xffffff, 1.3))
const sun = new DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 2.6)
sun.position.set(-1e4, -4e3, 7e3)
scene.add(sun)

const camera = new PerspectiveCamera(60, innerWidth / innerHeight, 1, 1e6)
camera.up.set(0, 0, 1)
camera.position.set(0, -1200, 900) // a 3 × 3 grid is 1800 units wide

const renderer = new WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true })
renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2))
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight)
document.body.append(renderer.domElement)
const controls = new MapControls(camera, renderer.domElement)

const map = new Map({
  source: { api: 'eox' }, // Sentinel-2 imagery
  location: { lat: 46.57634, lon: 7.9904 }
})
scene.add(map.terrain)
await map.init()

renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => {
  controls.update()
  renderer.render(scene, camera)
})
```


### React Three Fiber


```tsx
function Terrain() {
  const map = useMemo(
    () =>
      new Map({
        source: { api: 'eox' },
        location: { lat: 46.57634, lon: 7.9904 }
      }),
    []
  )
  useEffect(() => {
    void map.init()
    return () => map.clean()
  }, [map])
  return <primitive object={map.terrain} />
}
// <Canvas camera={{ up: [0, 0, 1], position: [0, -1200, 900], far: 1e6 }}>
```


A pointer event already carries the hit:
`map.getLocation(map.terrain.worldToLocal(event.point.clone()))`.


### Positions and picking


```ts
const p = await map.getTerrainPosition({ lat, lon }) // on the rendered surface
const q = map.getTerrainPositionSync({ lat, lon }) // per frame; undefined until loaded
const r = map.getPosition({ lat, lon, alt: 3000 }) // at an altitude in meters
const { lat, lon, alt } = map.getLocation({ x, y, z }) // the inverse
const hit = map.pick(raycaster) // { lat, lon, alt, point } | undefined
```


### A city with layers


Layers need a city zoom (14–16) and true scale:


```ts
import {
  Buildings,
  Map,
  Roads,
  TerrainBase,
  Vegetation,
  Water
} from 'three-map-terrain'

const map = new Map({
  location: { lat: 46.515, lon: 6.632 },
  elevation: { api: 'mapterhorn' }, // finer than the default AWS tiles
  options: { zoom: 15, tileSegments: 64, exaggeration: 1, baseAltitude: 372 },
  material: { color: '#f2ede5' } // no imagery: a plain model
})
const buildings = map.addLayer(
  new Buildings({ source: { api: 'openfreemap' }, edges: true })
)
const roads = map.addLayer(new Roads({ source: { api: 'openfreemap' } }))
const water = map.addLayer(new Water({ source: { api: 'openfreemap' } }))
map.addLayer(
  new Vegetation({
    source: { api: 'openfreemap' },
    avoid: [water, roads, buildings]
  })
)
map.addLayer(new TerrainBase())
scene.add(map.terrain)
await map.init()
map.focus = controls.target // layers draw what the camera looks at first

const hit = buildings.pick(raycaster) ?? roads.pick(raycaster) // { feature, lat, lon, alt, point }
buildings.highlight(hit?.feature)
```


Layers using the same preset share its tiles. Below a layer's `minZoom`
(Buildings 13, Roads 12, Water 10, Vegetation 14) it draws nothing.


### Sources


- Imagery `source`: `{ api: 'eox' | 'osm' | 'none' }`,
  `{ api: 'mapbox' | 'maptiler', token }`, any `{ url: '…/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg',
maxZoom, attribution }` (`{-y}`, `{s}`, `{quadkey}` too), or
  `{ load: ({ z, x, y, signal }) => image | canvas | bitmap }`.
- `elevation`: `{ api: 'aws' }` (default), `'mapterhorn'`,
  `{ api: 'mapbox' | 'maptiler', token }`, `{ url, encoding: 'terrarium' |
'mapbox' | (r, g, b) => meters }`, or a `load` returning RGBA pixels.
- A layer's `source`: `{ api: 'openfreemap' | 'versatiles' }`,
  `{ api: 'maptiler' | 'mapbox' | 'protomaps', token }`, `{ api: 'overpass' }`
  (every OSM tag, slow — tens of seconds a tile), `{ url | tilejson, layers,
properties }` for any MVT server, `{ tiles: new VectorTiles(…) }` to share
  your own, or `{ minZoom, maxZoom, load: async ({ z, x, y, signal }) =>
features }`. `properties` (and `query` for Overpass) read more than the
  defaults.
- Missing tiles (404, `load` → `null`) and zooms beyond `maxZoom` are cut out
  of an ancestor.


### Materials


- The look, shared by the terrain and its layers: `material: { color,
lights, wireframe, fillOpacity, fog }` on the map; a layer's `material`
  overrides it.
- `process: (context, { width, height }) => void` draws on a tile's
  imagery (canvas 2D) before it becomes a texture — tones, overlays.
- `create: ({ texture, tile, options }) => Material` makes the terrain's
  material (PBR, shaders, node materials). The tile owns the texture: never
  dispose it through the material.
- A layer's `material`: a `Material` for all faces, or
  `(part) => Material | undefined` per part — Buildings `walls`, `roofs`,
  `floors`, `edges`; Roads `surface`, `rails`, `deck`, `structure`, `lines`;
  Water `water`, `lines`; Vegetation `crowns`, `trunks`, `bushes`. UVs are in
  meters. Materials you pass are never disposed by the layer. A material
  lying on the terrain needs `polygonOffset: true, polygonOffsetFactor: -1,
polygonOffsetUnits: -4`.
- At runtime: `map.setSource(…)`, `map.setMaterial({ … })`,
  `layer.setMaterial(…)` — geometry is kept.


### A layer of your own


```ts
const pins = map.addLayer(
  new FeatureLayer<Pin>({
    name: 'pins',
    source: {
      minZoom: 15,
      maxZoom: 15,
      load: async ({ z, x, y, signal }) => fetchPins(z, x, y, signal)
    },
    material: { color: '#ff5a36' },
    build(ctx) {
      const [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] = ctx.rect
      for (const pin of ctx.allFeatures) {
        const [x, y] = ctx.toLocal(pin.position) // [lon, lat] → tile coordinates
        if (x < minX || x >= maxX || y < minY || y >= maxY) continue // another tile's
        ctx.feature(pin, () => {
          ctx
            .instances('pins', geometry)
            .add(new Matrix4().setPosition(x, y, ctx.groundAt(x, y)))
        })
      }
    }
  })
)
pins.pick(raycaster)?.feature
```


`ctx` also has `drapePolygon`, `drapeLine`, `drapePath`, `extrude`, `face`,
`segment`, `add(object)`, `surfaceAt`, `unitsPerMeter`, `zScale`. Geometry
for `ctx.instances` needs a white `color` attribute to take the part's
color. Built-in layers take `build(ctx, draw)` to replace the geometry of
some features. Anything that is not tile features implements `MapLayer`
(`attach`, `tileLoaded`, `tileChanged`, `tileRemoved`, `detach` — all
optional).


### Export


```ts
const blob = await map.export('glb') // 'glb' | 'gltf' | 'obj' | 'stl' | 'usdz'
```


Waits for everything, in meters; options `textures`, `lines`, `layers`,
`units: 'scene'`. For 3D printing: a `TerrainBase`, STL, and leave the roads
out.


### Large areas


- An area of any shape: `grid` from `Utils.position2tile(lat, lon, zoom)` of
  its corners.
- Streaming: `map.addTileSegment(x, y)` / `map.removeTileSegment(x, y)`
  around the camera's target; give `Buildings` `clip: false`.
- Levels of detail: maps of different zooms, `ring.alignTo(detail)`, and
  `skirt` (meters) to close the steps; `nTiles: 0` when adding tiles one by
  one.


### Performance


`tileSegments` (48–64 at city zooms), `imageryZoomOffset` (0: a quarter of
the imagery), layers' `maxDistance` (meters, or per part), `map.focus`,
Roads `kinds`, Vegetation `spacing` / `maxPerTile`, a pixel ratio of at most 2.


## Pitfalls


- Black or flat-looking terrain: no lights (or `lights: false` wanted).
- Nothing visible: `camera.up` not Z, a far plane under ~1e5, or
  `map.terrain` not added.
- Buildings squashed or tall: `exaggeration` not set at a city zoom.
- Empty layers: a zoom below their `minZoom`, or a slow Overpass still
  loading.
- Credits: show `map.attributions` with the map. `eox` (Sentinel-2 2016) is
  non-commercial (CC BY-NC-SA); OpenStreetMap's tile servers and the public
  Overpass instances are for light use.
- Positions from a moved `map.terrain`: convert with `worldToLocal` first.
- Works with `WebGPURenderer` too: the library uses only built-in materials.
````

# Lower-level exports

> Tile math, the Tile class, textures, the drawing builders, schema readers of every layer, the MVT decoder and the model exporter.

* `Utils` — Web Mercator tile math: `position2tile`, `position2tileFraction`, `tile2bbox`, `tile2lat`, `tile2lon`, `tile2position`, `tileWidth`, `getTileKey`.
* `Tile` — one terrain tile: elevation decoding, geometry, seams, `heightAt(u, v)`, `updateGeometry(rows?, columns?)` (after changing heights: normals around the vertices changed, bounds), `children()`, `loadImagery()`, `loadTexture()`, `whenTextured()`, `restyle()`, `dispose()`.
* `loadQuadTexture`, `createTerrainMaterial` — the 2 × 2 child-tile texture and the built-in material made from it.
* `TileContext`, `TileSurface` (heights and normals of a tile, as the GPU interpolates them), `SurfaceBuilder`, `LineBuilder`, `InstanceBuilder`, `FEATURE_ATTRIBUTE` — what layers draw with.
* `buildingsFromVectorTile`, `readBuildings`, `openMapTilesProperties`, `mapboxStreetsProperties`, `protomapsProperties`, `shortbreadProperties`, `overtureProperties` — buildings from vector tiles, by schema; `buildingsFromOverpass`, `overpassQuery`, `osmBuildingAttributes`, `LEVEL_HEIGHT` — from OpenStreetMap.
* `roadsFromVectorTile`, `readRoads`, `openMapTilesRoadProperties`, `mapboxStreetsRoadProperties`, `protomapsRoadProperties`, `shortbreadRoadProperties`, `roadKind`, `ROAD_KINDS`, `ROAD_WIDTHS`, `LINK_WIDTH` — roads from vector tiles; `roadsFromOverpass`, `overpassRoadsQuery`, `osmRoadAttributes`, `LANE_WIDTH` — from OpenStreetMap.
* `waterFromVectorTile`, `readWater`, `openMapTilesWaterProperties` (and the Mapbox, Protomaps, Shortbread ones), `WATERWAY_WIDTHS`, `WATER_COLOR`; `waterFromOverpass`, `overpassWaterQuery` — water.
* `vegetationFromVectorTile`, `readVegetation`, `openMapTilesVegetationProperties` (and the others), `BUSH_KINDS`, `isBush`, `CROWN_COLOR`, `BUSH_COLOR`, `TRUNK_COLOR`, `plantShapes`; `vegetationFromOverpass`, `overpassVegetationQuery` — vegetation.
* `parseLength`, `toNumber`, `clipRect`, `isRing`, `Position`, `Ring` — reading features.
* `decodeVectorTile`, `gunzip` — the vector tile (MVT) decoder.
* `exportModel`, `MODEL_TYPES`, `expandTileUrl`.

Every export is documented in the package’s type declarations: [`dist/index.d.ts`](https://unpkg.com/three-map-terrain/dist/index.d.ts).

# Layer members

> The members every layer shares — pick, highlight, setMaterial, maxDistance, the ground it covers — and new FeatureLayer(), the frame of them all.

The options of each layer are on its page: [`Buildings`](/three-map-terrain/layers/buildings/#new-buildings-source-options-), [`Roads`](/three-map-terrain/layers/roads/#new-roads-source-options-), [`Water`](/three-map-terrain/layers/water/#new-water-source-options-), [`Vegetation`](/three-map-terrain/layers/vegetation/#new-vegetation-source-options-), [`TerrainBase`](/three-map-terrain/layers/base/#new-terrainbase-depth-material-).

## `new FeatureLayer({ source, build?, material?, highlightColor?, minZoom?, maxDistance?, name? })`

The frame of the layers — [Your own layers](/three-map-terrain/own-layers/). `source` is any `FeatureSource`; `name` names the group and its objects (`'<name> <part> <z/x/y>'`).

## Members

The layers share these members:

| Member                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pick(raycaster)`, `pickIntersection(intersection)` | `{ feature, lat, lon, alt, point }` of the feature hit — never one behind the terrain                                                                                                                                                      |
| `highlight(feature \| id, color?)`                  | Draws a feature over its material; a feature with an `id` is highlighted in every tile; no argument clears it                                                                                                                              |
| `setMaterial(material)`                             | A look merged into the layer’s, or a material or a function replacing it — changed in place                                                                                                                                                |
| `invalidate(tiles?)`                                | Draws the tiles again                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `whenReady()`                                       | Resolves once the layer’s data is loaded and drawn                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `maxDistance`                                       | Meters from the camera beyond which a tile’s objects are hidden (`(part) => meters \| undefined` per part), measured to the nearest point of its terrain before every render, changeable any time (objects of `ctx.add()` are left to you) |
| `count`                                             | Features drawn (a feature crossing tiles counts once per tile)                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `group`                                             | The layer’s objects, in `map.terrain`                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `source`, `attribution`                             | Where its features come from, and their credit                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `dispose()`                                         | Frees what the layer made                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

And the ground they take (`GroundCover`, what `Vegetation`’s `avoid` reads):

| Member                  | Description                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `covers(x, y, margin?)` | Whether their faces, seen from above, cover a point in map units (tiles at the map’s zoom), or come within `margin` of it |
| `onTileDrawn(listener)` | Told about every tile drawn again or removed; returns how to stop                                                         |
| `pending(tile)`         | Whether a tile is still to be drawn — its data loading or its drawing queued (optional for your own)                      |

## `MapLayer`

What the map talks to — every method optional: `attribution`, `attach(map)`, `tileLoaded(tile)`, `tileChanged(tile)`, `tileRemoved(tile)`, `materialChanged(map)`, `whenReady()`, `detach(map)`. [Your own layers](/three-map-terrain/own-layers/#maplayer).

# Map

> new Map() — its props, MapOptions and material options — and its members, from init() and positions to layers, export, streaming and clean().

## `new Map({ location, source?, elevation?, options?, material? })`

| Prop        | Type                                      | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `location`  | `{ lat: number; lon: number }`            | Its tile is the origin of the coordinates, and the middle of the `nTiles` grid              |
| `source`    | `Source \| SourceProps`                   | Imagery; [see Sources](/three-map-terrain/sources/#imagery--source). Without it, none       |
| `elevation` | `ElevationSource \| ElevationSourceProps` | Elevation; [AWS Terrain Tiles](/three-map-terrain/sources/#elevation--elevation) by default |
| `options`   | `Partial<MapOptions>`                     | See below                                                                                   |
| `material`  | `Partial<TerrainMaterialOptions>`         | [Materials](/three-map-terrain/materials/#options)                                          |

### `MapOptions`

Defaults in `defaultMapOptions`.

| Option              | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nTiles`            | `3`     | The grid is `nTiles × nTiles` tiles                                                                                                                                                              |
| `grid`              | —       | The grid as any rectangle of tiles at `zoom` instead, inclusive: `{ minX, minY, maxX, maxY }` (`nTiles` is ignored). [Large areas](/three-map-terrain/large-areas/)                              |
| `zoom`              | `11`    | Zoom level of the terrain tiles; the imagery’s is `zoom + imageryZoomOffset`                                                                                                                     |
| `tileSize`          | `600`   | Size of a tile in scene units                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `tileSegments`      | `100`   | Segments per tile side (`PlaneGeometry`), 1–256                                                                                                                                                  |
| `zScale`            | `0.045` | Scene units per meter of elevation. True scale is `tileSize / Utils.tileWidth(lat, zoom)`; the default is true scale at zoom 11 around 46°                                                       |
| `exaggeration`      | —       | Vertical exaggeration relative to true scale (`1`: true to scale); when set, it decides `zScale`                                                                                                 |
| `baseAltitude`      | `0`     | Altitude in meters drawn at z = 0                                                                                                                                                                |
| `imageryZoomOffset` | `1`     | A tile is textured with `4^offset` imagery tiles stitched into one: `0` its own (a quarter of the requests and memory), `1` its four children, `2` sixteen (sharper); 0–3                        |
| `skirt`             | `0`     | Meters a strip hangs straight down from every tile’s edge, in its material: it closes the steps to another map ([levels of detail](/three-map-terrain/large-areas/#levels-of-detail)); `0`: none |

## Members

Positions are in `map.terrain` coordinates: X east, Y north, Z up. Transforms of `map.terrain` (or its parents) are taken into account by `pick`.

| Member                                                                    | Returns                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `terrain`                                                                 | `Group`                                 | Add it to your scene; one mesh per loaded tile, and the layers’ objects                                                                                                                   |
| `focus`                                                                   | `Vector3 \| undefined`                  | Where the layers draw first, in world coordinates — e.g. `camera.position` or the controls’ `target`, followed as it moves; by default the location                                       |
| `init(callback?)`                                                         | `Promise<void>`                         | Loads the grid. Resolves (and calls `callback`, sets `ready`) once every tile has its elevation and seams are stitched; textures keep streaming in. Calls before `clean()` share one load |
| `whenReady()`                                                             | `Promise<void>`                         | Resolves once everything is loaded: tiles, their textures, the layers’ content                                                                                                            |
| `getPosition({ lat, lon, alt }, { loadTile })`                            | `{ x, y, z }`                           | `x`, `y` of a geolocation, `z = (alt − baseAltitude) × zScale`. Loads the tile if it is not in the grid, unless `loadTile: false`                                                         |
| `getTerrainPosition({ lat, lon })`                                        | `Promise<{ x, y, z }>`                  | A point exactly on the rendered surface, interpolated over the mesh triangles. Waits for (and loads) the tile; rejects if it cannot be loaded                                             |
| `getTerrainPositionSync({ lat, lon }, { loadTile })`                      | `{ x, y, z } \| undefined`              | The same, synchronously: `undefined` while the tile is not loaded (starts loading it unless `loadTile: false`)                                                                            |
| `getLocation({ x, y, z })`                                                | `{ lat, lon, alt }`                     | Inverse of `getPosition`; `alt` in meters                                                                                                                                                 |
| `pick(raycaster)`                                                         | `{ lat, lon, alt, point } \| undefined` | The terrain hit by a ray, e.g. after `raycaster.setFromCamera(pointer, camera)`; `point` in world coordinates                                                                             |
| `setSource(source)`                                                       | `void`                                  | Replaces the imagery (`{ api: 'none' }` turns it off); each tile keeps its texture until the new one arrives                                                                              |
| `setMaterial(options)`                                                    | `void`                                  | Changes the material options of the terrain and the layers that follow it — their materials, in place; a new `process` reloads the imagery                                                |
| `addLayer(layer)`, `removeLayer(layer)`, `layers`                         |                                         | [Layers](/three-map-terrain/layers/): buildings, roads, base, yours. Layers survive `clean()`                                                                                             |
| `export(format?, options?)`                                               | `Promise<Blob>`                         | [A model file](/three-map-terrain/export/) of everything                                                                                                                                  |
| `attributions`                                                            | `string[]`                              | The credits of the sources and layers in use — show them with the map                                                                                                                     |
| `bounds`, `grid`                                                          |                                         | The grid as `[west, south, east, north]` in degrees, and in tiles                                                                                                                         |
| `addTileSegment(x, y)`                                                    | `Promise<void>`                         | Loads one more tile of the grid’s zoom                                                                                                                                                    |
| `removeTileSegment(x, y)`                                                 | `boolean`                               | Removes a tile: the layers let go of it, a pending load is aborted, its resources freed. Whether there was one. [Streaming](/three-map-terrain/large-areas/#streaming)                    |
| `alignTo(map)`                                                            | `void`                                  | Sets the transform of `terrain` so that this map lines up with another — any zoom, tile size, vertical scale. [Levels of detail](/three-map-terrain/large-areas/#levels-of-detail)        |
| `clean()`                                                                 | `void`                                  | Removes the tiles, aborts pending requests, disposes geometries, materials and textures. `init()` can be called again                                                                     |
| `ready`, `options`, `materialOptions`, `tileCache`, `source`, `elevation` |                                         | Whether `init()` finished, the resolved options, the loaded `Tile`s by `z/x/y`, the sources                                                                                               |

With React Three Fiber, pointer events already carry the hit: `map.getLocation(map.terrain.worldToLocal(event.point.clone()))`.

# Source classes

> Source, ElevationSource, the layers' feature sources, VectorTiles and Overpass — the classes behind the props of every source.

* `new Source(props)` — imagery; `tileUrl(z, x, y)`, `load(tile)`.
* `new ElevationSource(props)` — elevation; `tileUrl(z, x, y)`, `load(tile)`, `decode(r, g, b)`; `decodeTerrarium`, `decodeMapbox`.
* `new BuildingSource(props)`, `new RoadSource(props)`, `new WaterSource(props)`, `new VegetationSource(props)` — features read through `buildingSchema`, `roadSchema`, `waterSchema`, `vegetationSchema`; `load(tile)`, `tiles`. All are `TileFeatureSource`s.
* `new VectorTiles(props)` — a vector tile provider (`api`, `url` or `tilejson`, `schema`); `load(tile)` → `VectorTileData` with `layer(name)`; `VectorTiles.preset(api, token?)` is the instance layers share.
* `new Overpass({ endpoint? })` — `query(ql, signal)`, one request at a time per endpoint.

All take the props shown in [Sources](/three-map-terrain/sources/); `Map`, `Buildings`, `Roads` and the others also take the props directly.

A `FeatureSource` — what [your own layers](/three-map-terrain/own-layers/) take — is any object with `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, `attribution?` and `load(tile)` returning the features of a tile; `tile` is `{ z, x, y, signal }`.

# Data and attribution

> The credits and terms of the elevation, imagery and OpenStreetMap data the presets use — show map.attributions with the map.

Show the credits of the data you use — `map.attributions` lists them — and follow its terms. Exported models carry the data’s license too.

* AWS Terrain Tiles: [sources and attribution](https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md). Mapterhorn: [attribution](https://mapterhorn.com/attribution).
* `eox`: [Sentinel-2 cloudless](https://s2maps.eu) by EOX IT Services GmbH (contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data). The 2016 layer used here is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial use.
* `osm` imagery: © OpenStreetMap contributors — mind the [tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/); heavy use needs your own tile server.
* Buildings and roads from OpenStreetMap (OpenFreeMap, VersaTiles, MapTiler, Mapbox, Protomaps, Overpass) and Overture are under the [ODbL](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright): credit OpenStreetMap contributors (and the Overture Maps Foundation). The public Overpass API instances are for moderate use: [their limits](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API#Public_Overpass_API_instances).
* swisstopo geodata: free with the credit © swisstopo.
* `mapbox`, `maptiler`, `protomaps`: their terms of service, with your token.
